name: @w6w-apps/coda
description: Read and write Coda docs, tables and rows via the Coda REST API.

w6w.longDescription:
Coda puts a doc's tables and rows into a workflow — list docs, tables and columns, read rows, and write to them with upsert, update or delete. Row writes queue asynchronously and return a request id; a separate action polls that id so a workflow can wait for an edit to actually land before reading the row back, rather than assuming a queued response means the change already happened.

Upsert is the one action worth knowing the shape of: without a set of key columns, every call inserts new rows, so retrying it duplicates them, while providing key columns makes it behave as a true upsert that converges on retry. Update and delete are idempotent either way — reapplying the same cell values, or deleting an already-gone row, lands on the same end state.

Authentication is a single API token generated from the account's own settings page, with no OAuth flow involved.
